summary: The old harness cannot reach printing of an object with a constructed cJSON_Raw member on either source version.

claims.necessity_reason: Printing an object containing a raw member is supported: cJSON_AddRawToObject creates that member, and the object printer passes it to print_value, which emits raw values. The harness prints only parsed trees. The complete parse_value dispatcher never creates cJSON_Raw, and the harness has no insertion step, so no fuzz input reaches this behavior.

before.requirement: Reach printing of an object containing a constructed cJSON_Raw member value.
before.reason: The object printer passes each member to print_value, which supports cJSON_Raw. Parsing cannot create that type, and the old harness performs no member construction.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: print_value emits a cJSON_Raw member's valuestring.
The complete value dispatcher has no path that creates cJSON_Raw from input text.
cJSON_AddRawToObject provides a supported way to construct the object member.

after.requirement: Reach printing of an object containing a constructed cJSON_Raw member value.
after.reason: The raw member printing route remains supported. The same old harness still prints only parsed trees, whose members cannot have cJSON_Raw type.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: print_value still emits a cJSON_Raw member's valuestring.
The complete value dispatcher still has no path that creates cJSON_Raw from input text.
cJSON_AddRawToObject still provides a supported way to construct the object member.

claims.comparison_reason: On both sides, the old harness obtains its printed tree solely through parsing and never inserts a raw object member.
